pages.name: Combat Round
pages.html:
Vehicular Combat: Vehicular combat happens alongside normal combat and uses the same range bands for ranged weapons. Use the following to help integrate vehicles into combat encounters.

Combat Round: Vehicular combat rounds are ten seconds and follow the same procedure as normal combat rounds. See Combat pg. 41 for more information.

Book p.49

pages.name: Declare Movement and Actions
pages.html:
• Vehicular positioning: Vehicles gain the same advantage from positioning as characters and NPCs with relation to cover and elevation.
  • Vehicular movement: Vehicles move at the same time as characters and NPCs do in a combat round. During movement, it is possible to hit a character or NPC target as part of the movement phase.

Book p.49

pages.name: Vehicular Attacks
pages.html:
Attack: Apply the difference in speed bands between attacker and defender as a -DM to the attacker.

Book p.49

pages.name: Vehicular Damage
pages.html:
Damage: Any time a vehicle takes damage, roll on the following table to determine the location of the damage.

Vehicular damage from different types of attackers

  • Vehicle Weapon Damage: Roll the weapon die and apply it to the determined hit location.
  • Vehicle Weapon Damage to NPC: Vehicle weapon damages deals 6 damage to an NPC for every 1 vehicle damage
  • Character/NPC Weapon: Any rolled weapon dice only deal minimal 1 damage against a vehicle.
  • Starship Weapon: Any starship weapon damage instead deals 6 damage to a vehicle for every 1 point of damage it would inflict on a starship. For example, a starship firing its turret at a ground car would inflict 6 damage.

Book p.49

pages.name: Vehicle Mounted Weapons
pages.html:
Vehicle Mounted Weapons: All mounted weapons require a gunner to use them properly. The following weapons are only some examples for use with the same vehicles described in this book. Referees are encouraged to create their own to suit their needs if they desire more military-focused vehicles.

Range band: All vehicle weapons have Long Distance.

Tech level: All of the listed weapons are at Tech Level 7.

pages.name: Damage Locations
pages.html:
• Interior: Interior represents the control interface that is contained within the hull of a vehicle. Any interior hit harms the occupants. When occupants are hit, then weapon damage inflicts 1D per damage point of vehicular damage. If the interior reaches 0, then the vehicle cannot be controlled anymore and excessive damage is applied to the hull.
  • Drive: This represents the locomotion of the vehicle and its ability to maintain movement. Any damage done to drive reduces the vehicle's speed band by this amount. On zero, the vehicle cannot move and any additional hit goes to the hull.
  • Handling: If the power system is hit, decrease the handling by one per point of damage. In addition, the furthest distance the vehicle can travel is reduced by 20%. Once the handling reaches 0, then the vehicle’s power system is destroyed. Roll 1D. A roll of 4+ causes the vehicle to explode, dealing 6D damage to all occupants. Any excessive damage to the handling transfer to the hull.
  • Hull: This is the physical structure of the vehicle. On a Hull of 0, the structural integrity is compromised. Any hits to the hull causes the vehicle to explode on a 4+ on 1D dealing 6D damage to all occupants. Apply any additional hull damage taken as a +DM to the 1D die roll.
  • Weapon: If the vehicle has a weapon system, it is represented by this. All vehicle weapons deal their assigned weapon damage on a successful attack. All installed weapons only have one hit. Once a weapon system is hit, it cannot be used. Any additional hits to the weapon category is considered hull damage.
  • Armour: Armour reduces damage from other weapons by -1 when hit in the armoured location. Any vehicle that comes with an armour rating has 1 rating assigned to one of the different damage locations the vehicle has. A location cannot have more than 1 armour unless the vehicle’s armour rating exceeds armourable locations. For example, an ATV with armour 3 can only have the armour equipped to three of the five available locations for a military vehicle. An armoured hull does not protect against excessive damage from another damage location.

Book p.49

pages.name: Vehicular Combat Actions
pages.html:
• Ramming: Damage done to a target vehicle is equal to the speed band difference between the attacker and defender. The defender vehicle takes the entirety of the damage while the ramming vehicle will take damage equal to 1/2 the applied damage, rounded up.
  • Evade: This action is the same as evade but the vehicle’s required Skill must be applied.
  • Hit-and-run: If a character or NPC target is about to be hit by a vehicle, they can make a contested DEX check against the vehicle operator’s Drive Skill as long as they are not pinned (END 0). On a success, they avoid being hit. On a failure, the target is hit and takes damage equal to 1D per speed band the vehicle is moving at plus 1 per tonne the vehicle weighs. For example, a ground car that is driving at speed band 2 would deal 2D+2 damage to a person.
  • Offensive driving: A driver can bump a vehicle out of control by making a contested Drive check against the driver of the target vehicle, where the attacker adds +1DM for every 2 tonnes of weight their vehicle has above the target vehicle. If the attacker fails, they lose speed bands equal to the difference of the failed roll. If the target fails, they instead must make another drive check with a -DM equal to the difference to maintain operation of the vehicle. Failure to do so causes it to spin out. If there is any debris, other vehicle, or terrain within 5 metres, then it will crash into it. However, if the defending driver rolls a 2 or less, the vehicle flips overs and tumbles.

Book p.49
